words.engDef: so strange that it seems imaginary
words.example: The special effects in the movie were so good, they made the fantasy world seem almost unreal.
words.chinese: 不真實的；虛幻的；難以置信的

words.engDef: having no connection with something else
words.example: The two incidents appear to be completely unrelated.
words.rootPrefix: un- (not) + re- (back) + lat (to carry, from latus carried)

words.engDef: not stated exactly
words.example: The exact location of the new office is currently unspecified.
words.chinese: 未指明的；未詳細說明的；未經特別指定的

words.engDef: not common; different from what is normal
words.example: It's unusual for him to be late for a meeting, he's usually very punctual.
words.chinese: 不尋常的；異常的；非凡的

words.engDef: the tendency to change from one time to another
words.example: The data showed high variability in customer preferences.
words.chinese: 變異性；易變性；不穩定性

words.engDef: a form of something that differs slightly from others
words.example: The company released a new software variant with improved security features.
words.chinese: 變體；異體；變種；變型；差異形式；不同版本

words.engDef: the checking that something is true or accurate
words.example: The department implemented innovative verification procedures to improve operational efficiency.

words.engDef: the power to make your own choices
words.example: He made the decision of his own volition, without any pressure from others.

words.engDef: a turning point after which things are different
words.example: The discovery of penicillin was a watershed moment in medical history.
words.chinese: 分水嶺；轉捩點；重要關頭

words.engDef: by which means
words.example: They developed a new system whereby employees can submit their expenses online.

words.engDef: while
words.example: I often listen to music whilst I am working.
words.chinese: 當...的時候；與...同時；然而；儘管

words.engDef: completely
words.example: The success of the project was not wholly unexpected.
words.rootPrefix: hal (sound, healthy, akin to heal and health) + -ly

words.engDef: in a sensible and well-judged way
words.example: She wisely invested her savings in a diversified portfolio.

words.engDef: the taking out of money; also the act of pulling back
words.example: The bank processed the client's large withdrawal request within standard security protocols.
